_readme: Frozen inventory of consumer files and CSS selectors that SHADOW this module.
Enforced by tests/override-parity.spec.ts as a one-way ratchet: anything new
fails, and anything removed from a consumer must also be removed here.
Regenerate the raw numbers with `npm run scan:overrides`, but do NOT
bulk-overwrite this file — each line is an accepted exception, and the point
of the ratchet is that adding one is a deliberate, reviewed act.
Prose for every entry lives in OVERRIDES.md; the spec checks the two agree.
duplicatedSelectors counts REAL conflicts only: the consumer and extras set
at least one property in common. A selector they merely share the NAME of —
extras' `.hextra-toc { display: none }` versus a Tailwind `font-family` on the
same class — is not duplication and is no longer listed. Confusing the two is
what made 'four of six consumers override .hextra-toc' look like a real
backlog item when nobody overrides it.
An entry here is an ACCEPTED shadow, NOT necessarily a permanent one. Six are
scheduled removals whose verdict is already measured (see OVERRIDES.md): three
on docs, two on agentgateway-oss-website, one on kagent-oss-website. Listing
them is what makes the ratchet's second arm work: the day a consumer deletes
one, the 'stale' assertion fails and forces this file to be edited, so the
follow-up cannot be forgotten a second time. Leaving them OUT was the mistake
— an always-red spec is a spec everyone learns to skip. That applies to a
shadow whose verdict is DELETE just as much as to one whose verdict is KEEP:
the 'added' arm cannot track a deletion, only the 'stale' arm can, so
withholding an entry to 'keep tracking it' tracks strictly less.
